reviews.review: Good game. Better than ME 1, 2 and 3 IMO as more freedom of movements and specialisation and weapons and armors. A good 100 hours of play if you do all the quests and side-quests and take the time to read all the dialogues. More quests and side quests to do than No Man's Sky or Starfield as they both feel very empty compare to Andromeda.

I remember seeing this game get pilloried online after its release due to the numerous bugs, painfully awkward animations, and occasionally cringeworthy dialogue, and I avoided getting this game at first for those reasons. After finishing the Legendary version of the first ME trilogy, I was naturally left hungering for more, so I bit the bullet and got Andromeda. 

And I'm glad I did!

You can't patch the awkward dialogue and the main villain kinda seems like a cartoony villain compared to the previous ME games, but there is a lot of great fun and action to be had in this game. Many of the initial technical issues have been fixed, with a few exceptions – running through a level stuck in a T-pose is hilarious but just a tad bit difficult. Don't let that stop you, though – the game usually runs very well. There's enough content and side missions to keep you busy for awhile exploring the beautifully rendered solar systems in the galaxy, and the flexibility of the different warrior system types allows for different and unique playstyles.

Like other players have said: if you're looking for an experience on the same level as the original ME trilogy, you might not find all that you're looking for – but if you're willing to start a new adventure in this universe with a new crew, do not hesitate to give Andromeda a try.
